medium.clue: Furry companion that purrs on your lap.

hard.clue: It always lands on its feet.

rule_bad: For WOULD, answering "I would if it rained tomorrow" — WOULD itself must never appear in the clue text, even as part of a sentence.
"third person singular present tense of a verb" for a verb form.
For FAIRIES, "Plural of 'fairy'" — naming the grammatical operation (pluralization) and repeating the singular form is still a label, not a clue.
For TEE, "Word that starts with T and ends with EE." — that describes how the word is written, not what it means.

For WAS — first/third person singular PAST of "to be" — answering "We celebrated the end of exams" or "They were no longer the same after the trip": both describe a past state but neither is singular ("we"/"they" need WERE, not WAS), so neither fits.

For SUNG — past PARTICIPLE of "sing" (used with a helper verb, e.g. "has sung") — answering "The bird sang at dawn" (that's the simple past, SANG): wrong form — the clue must itself imply a helper verb, e.g. "What a choir has done by the end of the concert", not a stand-alone past-tense action.

For WILL — future modal auxiliary — answering "What lies hide" (a timeless present-tense statement): the clue itself must carry future framing (e.g. "What tomorrow holds") to match a word that specifically marks futurity, not a generic present-tense description.

For MICE — PLURAL (irregular: mouse → mice) — answering "A small rodent": that describes ONE mouse, not several — the clue must itself refer to more than one to fit a plural word, e.g. "Small rodents said to play while the cat's away."

For MIGHT — modal verb expressing possibility ("it might rain") — answering "Purchased at the corner shop": that has no connection at all to the meaning of possibility, it is simply a different, unrelated idea.

For SOWED — simple PAST of "sow" (to plant seeds) — answering "The act of scattering seeds into the earth" (a generic infinitive-style definition, no tense of its own): the clue itself must carry past-tense framing to match, e.g. "What a farmer did to every furrow last spring."

For FELLED — simple PAST of "fell" (to cut down) — answering "She would chop it down... wait, no, she felled it with one clean blow": the visible self-correction ("would chop it down... wait, no") is exactly what must never appear in a clue — decide on the final answer entirely before writing anything down, and write only "She felled it with one clean blow", never the discarded first attempt too.

For LAUGHS — third person singular PRESENT of "laugh", "he/she laughs" — answering "What you do when a joke pleases you": wrong person — "you" (second person) instead of "he/she" (third person), even though the meaning itself is right — the clue must itself be framed for the correct subject, e.g. "What she does when a joke pleases her."

For OWLS — PLURAL of "owl" — answering "owls - nocturnal birds of prey": labeling the answer with a dash before the actual definition still gives the word away, exactly like writing it anywhere else in the clue would. Write only the definition itself, with nothing labeling it, e.g. "Nocturnal birds of prey."
rule_good: For FAIRIES, "Magical beings from folk tales." (in the correct plural form, per rule 4).
